item.title: Ousted Bangladeshi leader vows to return from exile despite facing a death sentence
item.description: Hasina's speech marked the second anniversary of her ouster. She fled Bangladesh by helicopter following nearly two months of protests in 2024 that left nearly 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.

item.title: Dr. Erica Schwartz confirmed as CDC director, filling a leadership vacuum
item.description: Schwartz takes command of a public health agency that has lost thousands of employees, amid layoffs, resignations and leadership turmoil.

item.title: How Trump made an estimated $2.2 billion during the first year of his second term
item.description: New York Times reporter Eric Lipton discusses his Pulitzer Prize-winning investigations into Trump's conflicts of interest and whether he's exploiting the power of the presidency for self-enrichment.

item.title: Judge reluctantly dismisses case against Oath Keepers militia group over Jan. 6 riot
item.description: A judge has granted the Justice Department's bid to drop a landmark case against leaders of the Oath Keepers, as former prosecutors warn about the dangers of denying the violence of Jan. 6.

item.title: Pakistan's ruling party leads in Kashmir vote despite boycott call by banned group
item.description: Candidates backed by twice-elected former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-N party have won 24 of the 34 seats decided in the first two phases of voting, the election commission, said Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: A 73-year-old retired nurse's decision to learn to write Tibetan language offers a glimpse into how some embrace their language and cultural identity in Tibet.

item.title: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan's Democratic primary for Senate
item.description: El-Sayed, an epidemiologist, backs Medicare for all and decries corporate money in politics. He beat Rep. Haley Stevens, whose supporters said she would have had a better chance in the fall.

item.title: U.S. missile stockpiles dwindle. And, FDA weighs approval of flu shots with mRNA tech
item.description: The U.S. Army's missile stockpile is dwindling and could take years to replenish. And, the Food and Drug Administration is deciding whether to approve a flu vaccine with mRNA technology.

item.description: Ukraine's depleted air defenses failed to stop any of Moscow's incoming missiles overnight.

item.title: Progressives see biggest win yet in Michigan, while Trump flexes power over GOP
item.description: Progressives notched major wins in Michigan, while voters in Missouri and Washington rejected insurgent Democrats. Meanwhile, Trump continued to flex his influence over the Republican Party.
